The NeuroSynth analysis is a broad meta-analytic map of studies containing the term 'social' and is not specifically on tasks measuring affiliation/attachment; it does not meet the local inclusion criteria AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

The NeuroSynth analysis does not specifically measure perception/understanding of the self and therefore fails PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Although the NeuroSynth map aggregates many social tasks, it is not a task-specific map demonstrating perception/understanding of others per se and does not clearly satisfy PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
Independent study contrast (Social > Non-social) is a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map on healthy adults directly measuring social processing.
The independent study manipulated presence of social content but did not specifically measure affiliation or attachment processes; it fails AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

The contrast isolates socialness of scenes and does not target self-related processing or self-judgments; PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 are not satisfied.

The Social > Non-social contrast involves viewing images containing people and social interactions and thus indexes perception/understanding of others at the perceptual/representational level; it meets global criteria and the local PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.

Whole-brain group-level contrast (SC vs SA) on self-related trait evaluation in healthy adults assesses social processing. Global and local inclusion criteria are met.

Emphatic Accuracy Task is a social cognitive task measuring perception and interpretation of others' emotions; the contrast (emotional > neutral) is a group-level whole-brain task-evoked map in healthy adults.

The analysis does not measure affiliation or attachment processes (no task elements like kinship, cooperation, or loved-one vs stranger contrasts). Missing required inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
The task requires reception of others' affective signals (continuous ratings of emotional intensity from videos) and the contrast is a whole-brain group-level map in healthy adults.

Primary analyses focus on perceiving others' emotions rather than self-related judgments; the contrast does not target self-perception. Missing required inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
The contrast measures neural responses to perceiving and understanding others' emotional states (emotional > neutral) in a whole-brain group analysis of healthy adults.
The neutral > emotional contrast is part of the same social-emotion task and is a whole-brain group-level map in healthy adults, thus relevant to social processing.

This analysis does not probe affiliation or attachment constructs (no kinship/cooperation/loved-one contrasts). Missing required inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

Even though this contrast highlights relatively higher activation for neutral clips, it stems from the social communication task (ratings of others' emotional displays) and is a whole-brain group-level result in healthy adults.
The contrast contrasts conditions of the social task but does not measure self-perception or self-related judgments. Missing required inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
This whole-brain contrast arises from participants perceiving others (neutral versus emotional) and thus relates to perception and understanding of others' states.
Modulation of BOLD by intra-individual variation in empathic accuracy directly indexes social cognitive processing; analysis is whole-brain, group-level in healthy adults.
This analysis measures empathic accuracy/mentalising, not affiliation or attachment processes. Missing required inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

Empathic accuracy depends on reception and interpretation of others' affective signals; the parametric modulation analysis is a whole-brain group map in healthy adults and thus meets social communication criteria.

The analysis targets accuracy in perceiving others' emotions rather than self-perception; it does not measure self-related processes. Missing required inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Intra-individual variation in empathic accuracy reflects participants' ability to perceive and understand others' emotional states; the analysis is whole-brain and group-level in healthy adults.
Negative modulation by Z-EA still concerns social cognitive processing (relations between brain activity and empathic accuracy) and is a whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults.

This analysis reflects variation in empathic accuracy/mentalising rather than affiliation or attachment constructs. Missing required inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Regions negatively modulated by empathic accuracy are still part of processing others' communicative affect; the analysis is a whole-brain group-level task map in healthy adults.
The analysis does not index self-related perception or judgments; it concerns accuracy in perceiving others. Missing required inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Negative relationship to Z-EA still pertains to perception and understanding of others (how brain activity varies with accuracy); the analysis is whole-brain and group-level in healthy adults.

Correlation between BOLD and participants' continuous ratings of targets' emotional intensity directly indexes social processing of others' emotions; whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults.

This analysis measures moment-to-moment perception of others' emotions, not attachment/affiliation constructs. Missing required inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

The analysis captures reception and processing of others' affective communication over time (continuous ratings), meeting social communication criteria and is a whole-brain group-level map in healthy adults.

Although participants reported their own feelings elsewhere, this specific analysis models ratings of the target (others), not self-perception. Missing required inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
This analysis directly measures perception and understanding of others' emotional intensity over time (continuous rating correlations) in a whole-brain, group-level sample of healthy adults.
Negative correlations with emotional intensity still relate to social processing (engagement/other-related processing) and derive from whole-brain group-level task analysis in healthy adults.

This analysis reflects decreases with emotional intensity and does not probe affiliation/attachment constructs. Missing required inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Negative correlations arise from the same social communication task (processing others' emotional signals); as a whole-brain group-level result it meets inclusion criteria for social communication.
This analysis concerns neural responses relative to perceived others' emotional intensity (not self-related processes). Missing required inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Negative correlations with emotional intensity relate to aspects of perceiving others' emotional states; analysis is whole-brain, group-level in healthy adults.
